title: Improve dedicated autoscaler fallback reporting and burst/throughput metrics tagging
author: Priya Shah
release_notes:
- Fix incorrect fallback reporting when burst throttle triggers.
- Include SLO and priority tags on throughput/fallback metrics for better per-customer chargeback and alerting.
- Improve unit coverage for autoscaler reporting edge cases.
body:
Problem / Motivation:
The dedicated autoscaler would sometimes report fallback events (fallback to lower-tier model or queued throughput fallback) without the correct context tags (priority, SLO-class, or burst vs sustained). That made it hard for SRE and Cost Ops to correlate incidents with customer SLAs and led to noisy alerts during sustained high load when tokenbucket smoothing interacted with emergency burst controls.

What this change does:
- Adds explicit tagging for fallback events with: priority_level, slo_class, fallback_reason (burst_throttle | throughput_fallback | capacity_shortage), and origin_fleet_id.
- Fixes a race in pkg/autoscaler/fallback.go where a late tokenbucket sample could overwrite the fallback reason; now we atomically set and persist the first triggering reason for a request batch.
- Adds a throughput-level metric throughput.fallback.count{priority, slo_class, reason} and a derived counter throughput.fallback.duration_seconds to represent recovered vs sustained fallbacks.
- Surface the fallback reasons in the dedicated console dashboard and emit correct labels to the metrics registry so downstream billing/alerting can filter.
- Adds end-to-end tests that run a mini-simulated fleet and assert metrics + tags under burst and sustained load patterns.

Summary of commits:
- 8f7a2d5: fix: atomicize fallback reason set to avoid overwrite during concurrent samples
- 9c1b4a0: feat(metrics): add throughput.fallback.count and throughput.fallback.duration_seconds with tags
- 4b2d9f1: perf: avoid map allocations in hot path when priority==default by reusing precomputed tagset
- 6e5f3d2: test: add integrative e2e for burst->fallback reporting scenario
- 2a7c3f8: ui: wire fallback reason into dedicated console dashboard

Files changed (high-level):
- pkg/autoscaler/fallback.go (core fallback logic)
- pkg/autoscaler/reporting.go (metrics tagging and emission helpers)
- pkg/autoscaler/reporting_test.go (unit tests for tag propagation and race cases)
- services/dedicated/autoscaler/manager.go (fleet-level event plumbing)
- observability/metrics/registry.go (register new metrics and update docstrings)
- console/dashboards/dedicated-fallbacks.yaml (dashboard panels + filters)
- infra/helm/values.yaml (optional metric filters for customers)
- tests/e2e/dedicated/fallback_scenarios.go (integration harness)
- go.mod / go.sum (minor deps bumped for testing harness)

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests: added coverage for race and tag propagation (pkg/autoscaler/reporting_test.go).
- Integration: e2e harness simulates tokenbucket smoothing and burst throttle; validated metrics emitted and tags present.
- CI: all checks pass on this branch (unit, integration, lint, e2e/dedicated).

Rollout plan:
- Feature is behind a runtime feature flag (autoscaler.report_fallbacks=true). The default remains off for customers on older Dedicated releases.
- Deploy to staging fleet next week, watch throughput.fallback.* metrics and compare counts with previous baseline for a week.
- Enable gradually on a small set of Dedicated customers for initial verification, then flip cluster-wide once signals are green.

Backward compatibility / Risks:
- No breaking API changes. Metrics tags are additive. Downstream alerting pipelines that assume a fixed label set should be reviewed (we added priority_level and slo_class labels).
- Small perf cost for tag allocation on first-run of a tagset; mitigated by precomputing common tagsets for default priority.

Related work:
- ENG-4823: dedicated autoscaler observability initiative (this PR implements the reporting portion).
- ENG-4901: SLO tagging for runtime events.

Acknowledgements:
Thanks to Marcus and Janelle for design reviews and to the CI/integration team for stabilizing the e2e harness used in tests.
